english: My name is Viktor.
My name is Oleg.
I read and write.
Brother rarely cooks lunch.
I love their family.
grammar: Свой means 'one's own' and refers back to the subject: Я люблю свою семью (I love my family).

english: I speak Russian well.
He speaks Russian well.
grammar: По-русски means 'in Russian' — the prefix по- with a language adjective describes how someone speaks: говорить по-русски.

english: She speaks Russian well.
grammar: Хорошо is an adverb meaning 'well.' Russian adverbs don't change form — they modify the verb directly.

english: Brother rarely does laundry.
Grandmother sometimes does laundry.
Grandmother usually washes dishes.
Sister runs every morning.
grammar: Бегать is a multidirectional verb of motion meaning 'to run regularly.' Каждое утро (every morning) signals habitual action.

english: Welcome to our city!
I walk to work.
grammar: Russian has no articles (a/the) — context determines definiteness.

english: During the day I work.
Mom runs in the afternoon.
What time is it now?
grammar: Который час? means 'What time is it?' — который (which) agrees in gender with час (hour, masculine).

english: I know the Russian language.
She knows the Russian language.
I read a book recently.
He works harder than everyone.
Mom rarely listens to music.
The journalist rarely buys groceries.
Grandmother rarely studies a language.
Grandfather sometimes writes a letter.
Mom watches a movie now.
grammar: Смотреть is a second conjugation verb: смотрю, смотришь, смотрит. The third-person form смотрит is used here with мама.

english: Brother sometimes cleans the apartment.
The farmer usually cooks lunch.
grammar: Готовить (to cook) is second conjugation: готовлю, готовишь, готовит. Note the consonant mutation л→вл in the first person.

english: Grandfather watches a movie now.
grammar: Сейчас (now/right now) indicates an action happening at this moment, requiring present tense.

english: Where is the nearest pharmacy?
grammar: Ближайшая is the superlative of близкий (near) — it agrees with аптека (feminine). Находится is a reflexive verb meaning 'is located.'

english: He knows the Russian language.
grammar: Знать (to know facts) takes accusative: русский язык. Compare with уметь (to know how) which takes infinitive.

english: Grandmother doesn't have a phone.
grammar: У + genitive + нет + genitive expresses 'not having': У бабушки нет телефона. Нет requires genitive case.

english: He thinks about his family.
grammar: О + prepositional means 'about': думать о семье. Своей is the prepositional feminine form of свой, agreeing with семья.

english: He works, and she studies.
grammar: А is a contrast conjunction meaning 'but/while': он работает, а она учится. It shows contrast without contradiction, unlike но (but).

english: I know that you can.
grammar: Что here means 'that' introducing a subordinate clause: Я знаю, что ты можешь. A comma always precedes что.

english: While he sleeps, she works.
grammar: Пока means 'while' for simultaneous actions: Пока он спит, она работает. Both clauses use present tense.

english: She inquired what I do.
Grandmother is eighty-five years old.
She came to work early.
She doesn't like cold weather.
grammar: Холодную погоду is accusative feminine — adjective + noun both change form as the direct object of любить.

english: I'm not cold, I'm hot.
Fresh bread is sold nowhere.
One, two, three, four, five.
grammar: After 2-4, use genitive singular: два стола (two tables), три книги (three books).

target: Разве ты не знал об этом?
english: Didn't you know about this?

target: Расскажи мне то, что ты знаешь.
english: Tell me what you know.
She writes with her left hand.
grammar: Левой рукой uses instrumental case to express 'with/by means of': she writes with (her) left hand.

english: The writer always listens to music.
The child turned one year old.
The sun rises early in summer.
grammar: Встаёт is from вставать (to get up/rise). Рано (early) and летом (in summer, instrumental) set the time context.

english: The teacher studies a language now.
grammar: Учить means 'to study/learn' or 'to teach' depending on context. Here учитель учит = the teacher teaches.

english: The doctor usually writes a letter.
grammar: Писать (to write) has a consonant mutation: пис- becomes пиш- in conjugation: пишу, пишешь, пишет.

english: The musician always watches a movie.
The chef usually helps a friend.
grammar: Помогать (to help) takes dative: помогает другу (helps a friend). Друг→другу is the dative form.

english: What time does the museum close?
Brother usually runs in the morning.
The teacher checks the students' notebooks.
How do you know my address?
I read a book every evening.
grammar: Каждый вечер (every evening) signals habitual action, requiring imperfective читаю. The accusative книгу marks the direct object.

english: Before sleep, he reads a book.
I think that he is right.
Mom listens to music every day.
Bye, see you tomorrow at work!
He turned forty years old yesterday.
grammar: Исполнилось + dative expresses age events: Ему исполнилось сорок лет = He turned forty. Note dative ему + past neuter исполнилось.

english: Today is the thirteenth — Friday.
We waited for about two hours.
He reads a book every evening.
grammar: First conjugation (-е-): читать → читаю, читаешь, читает, читаем, читаете, читают.

english: She reads a book every evening.
grammar: Читать is first conjugation: читаю, читаешь, читает. Here она читает — third person singular with the -ет ending.

english: My father works at a factory.
Grandmother always swims in the pool.
What do you want for dinner?
Do you have any available rooms?
Which of these restaurants is better?
The programmer commutes to work now.
My sister has two small children.
Please give three cups of tea.
grammar: After 1: nominative singular (один дом). After 2-4: genitive singular (два дома). After 5+: genitive plural (пять домов).

target: Отец покупает свежий хлеб каждое утро.
english: Father buys fresh bread every morning.

target: Не могли бы вы говорить немного медленнее?
english: Could you speak a little slower?

target: Я не хочу ни чай, ни кофе.
english: I want neither tea nor coffee.

target: У меня нет ни братьев, ни сестёр.
english: I have neither brothers nor sisters.
I write a letter to a friend.
She writes a letter to a friend.
grammar: Другу is dative of друг — with писать, the dative marks the recipient: пишет письмо другу (writes a letter to a friend).

english: I read a book in the morning.
I am looking for a good dentist.
It is three o'clock in the afternoon.
He works even if he is sick.
The read book is on the shelf.
grammar: Прочитанная is a past passive participle from прочитать: книга, которая была прочитана = a book that was read. It agrees with книга (fem.).

english: The temperature today is minus fifteen degrees.
grammar: Минус + number for negative temperatures: минус пятнадцать градусов. Numbers 5+ take genitive plural: градусов.

english: What time is it? Ten to two.
There are four books on the table.
Call me at seven in the evening.
I am trying to eat less sugar.
grammar: Меньше is the comparative of мало (little): есть меньше сахара = eat less sugar. Genitive сахара follows the comparative.

english: How much does a train ticket cost?
Why did you buy so much bread?
grammar: Зачем means 'what for/why (purpose)': Зачем ты купил? Столько + genitive means 'so much': столько хлеба.

target: Он работает в офисе каждый день.
english: He works in the office every day.

target: Она работает в офисе каждый день.
english: She works in the office every day.
grammar: В офисе uses prepositional case after в for location. Каждый день (every day) is accusative — time expressions often use accusative.

target: Я играю в парке по выходным.
english: I play in the park on weekends.

target: Он играет в парке по выходным.
english: He plays in the park on weekends.
grammar: Играть в + accusative for games/sports: играет в парке. По выходным (on weekends) uses dative plural with по.

target: Она играет в парке по выходным.
english: She plays in the park on weekends.
grammar: По выходным means 'on weekends' — по + dative plural expresses recurring time: по вечерам (in the evenings), по утрам (in the mornings).

target: Всё, что я знаю, я расскажу.
english: Everything that I know, I will tell.

target: Я знаю человека, который это сделал.
english: I know the person who did this.

target: Покажи мне место, где ты работаешь.
english: Show me the place where you work.

target: Вы говорите по-английски или только по-русски?
english: Do you speak English or only Russian?

target: Обед будет готов через двадцать минут.
english: Lunch will be ready in twenty minutes.

target: Завтрак подаётся с семи до десяти.
english: Breakfast is served from seven to ten.

target: Брат ездит на работу на велосипеде.
english: My brother rides his bicycle to work.

target: Отец готовит ужин для всей семьи.
english: Father cooks dinner for the whole family.
grammar: Для + genitive means 'for': для всей семьи. Всей is genitive feminine of весь (all/whole), agreeing with семья.

target: Она доехала до работы за час.
english: She got to work in an hour.

target: Врач ездит на работу по выходным.
english: The doctor commutes to work on weekends.
grammar: Ездить is a multidirectional verb of motion (by vehicle) for habitual trips: ездит на работу = commutes to work regularly.

target: Водитель ездит на работу после обеда.
english: The driver commutes to work after lunch.

target: Дети не должны гулять одни ночью.
english: Children should not walk alone at night.

target: Мне не удалось дозвониться до врача.
english: I couldn't reach the doctor by phone.

target: У меня есть брат и две сестры.
english: I have a brother and two sisters.

target: У меня два брата и три сестры.
english: I have two brothers and three sisters.
I've been waiting for half an hour already.
What do you need so much money for?
grammar: Зачем + dative means 'why do you need': Зачем тебе столько денег? Столько + genitive (денег) means 'so much/many.'

english: Allow me to introduce my colleague to you.
grammar: Позвольте (allow me) + infinitive is a formal way to introduce: Позвольте представить вам = Allow me to introduce to you. Вам is dative.

english: I write with a pen in a notebook.
She works and studies at the same time.
grammar: И means 'and' connecting two actions: работает и учится. Одновременно (simultaneously) is an adverb that doesn't change form.

english: The reading boy is sitting by the window.
grammar: Present active participle: -ущий/-ющий (1st conj.), -ащий/-ящий (2nd conj.): читающий (reading).

english: Our wedding is on the second of February.

target: Приветствую вас от имени нашей компании.
english: I greet you on behalf of our company.

target: Она читает детскую сказку перед сном.
english: She reads a children's fairy tale before bed.

target: Я хочу научиться готовить русские блюда.
english: I want to learn to cook Russian dishes.

target: Правда ли, что завтра будет снег?
english: Is it true that it will snow tomorrow?

target: Вы не знаете, во сколько открывается музей?
english: Do you know what time the museum opens?

target: Мы хотим пойти за грибами этой осенью.
english: We want to go mushroom picking this autumn.
grammar: За + instrumental means 'for/to gather': ходить за грибами = to go mushroom picking. This is a common Russian leisure activity.

target: Горячий чай с лимоном — лучшее лекарство.
english: Hot tea with lemon is the best medicine.

target: Как у тебя дела на работе в последнее время?
english: How are things at work for you lately?
While waiting for the bus, I read a newspaper.
grammar: Ожидая is an imperfective gerund from ожидать (to wait). Gerunds describe simultaneous actions: while waiting for the bus, I read.

english: The doctor works in the office in the evening.

target: Где вы работаете и чем занимаетесь?
english: Where do you work and what do you do?

target: Она работает врачом в городской больнице.
english: She works as a doctor at the city hospital.
grammar: Врачом uses instrumental case after работать to express profession: она работает врачом = she works as a doctor.

target: Он работает программистом в большой компании.
english: He works as a programmer at a large company.
grammar: Программистом is instrumental — Russian uses instrumental case after работать for professions: он работает программистом.

target: Мы хотим взять кота из приюта.
english: We want to adopt a cat from the shelter.
grammar: Из + genitive means 'from/out of': из приюта = from the shelter. Взять (to take) is perfective — they want to take (complete action).

target: Они хотят снять квартиру в центре.
english: They want to rent a flat in the centre.
grammar: В центре uses prepositional case for location. Снять квартиру means 'to rent an apartment' — a common collocation.

target: Мы встречаемся в шесть часов вечера.
english: We are meeting at six o'clock in the evening.
grammar: Который час? means 'What time is it?' — literally 'Which hour?'

target: Вы не подскажете дорогу к вокзалу?
english: Could you tell me the way to the station?
grammar: Не подскажете is a polite negative question form: 'Could you tell me?' Using не in questions makes requests more polite in Russian.

target: Вы не подскажете, где ближайшая аптека?
english: Could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?

target: Официант приносит меню и воду сразу.
english: The waiter brings the menu and water right away.

target: Старший брат помогает младшему с уроками.
english: The older brother helps the younger one with homework.

target: Коллега, с которой я работаю, очень умная.
english: The colleague with whom I work is very smart.

target: Слушай, ты не знаешь, где ближайшая аптека?
english: Listen, do you know where the nearest pharmacy is?

target: Он хочет найти работу ближе к дому.
english: He wants to find a job closer to home.
grammar: Ближе is the comparative of близко (near): ближе к дому = closer to home. К + dative means 'toward.'

target: С днём рождения! Вот тебе небольшой подарок.
english: Happy birthday! Here is a small gift for you.
grammar: С днём рождения! = Happy birthday! С + instrumental is used for congratulations: с Новым годом (Happy New Year).

target: Вы не знаете, есть ли тут рядом аптека?
english: Do you know if there is a pharmacy nearby?
grammar: Ли is a question particle used in indirect questions: есть ли тут рядом аптека = whether there is a pharmacy nearby.

target: Привет, мы сегодня идём в кино после работы.
english: Hi, we're going to the cinema after work today.
grammar: After работы (genitive) = after work. Идём is first person plural of идти — used for 'we are going' to a specific place.

english: Excuse me, how do I get to the train station?

target: В комнате четырнадцать стульев и один стол.
english: There are fourteen chairs and one table in the room.
grammar: Четырнадцать стульев: numbers 5+ take genitive plural. Стул has an irregular plural: стулья, genitive plural стульев.

target: Откуда вы и какой у вас родной язык?
english: Where are you from and what is your native language?

target: В библиотеке тысячи книг на разных языках.
english: There are thousands of books in different languages in the library.

target: Меня зовут Антон, я работаю учителем в школе.
english: My name is Anton, I work as a teacher at a school.

target: Добро пожаловать в наш город, здесь много интересного!
english: Welcome to our city, there is a lot of interesting things here!
What is your name?
Do you speak English?
Mom washes dishes soon.
Who wrote this book?
Brother often buys groceries.
I finished the work.
Mom usually plays chess.
She cannot come today.
Smoking is not allowed here.
The discount is fifteen percent.
Birds sing beautifully in spring.
grammar: Петь (to sing) has irregular conjugation: пою, поёшь, поёт, поём, поёте, поют. Красиво (beautifully) is an adverb.

english: The student usually does laundry.
Has he really already left?
grammar: Неужели is an emphatic question particle expressing surprise: 'Is it really true that...?' Уже means 'already.'

english: May I open the window?
Where can I buy souvenirs?
This is my brother's house.
Dad always reads a book.
Hi, let's meet after work.
We read about ancient history.
The neighbor usually plays chess.
grammar: Играть в + accusative for games: играет в шахматы (plays chess). В шахматы is always plural in Russian.

english: We don't need your help.
She hasn't read this book.
We have no available seats.
The girl usually cleans the apartment.
grammar: Убирать (to clean/tidy) is imperfective — обычно (usually) signals habitual action requiring imperfective aspect.

english: The nurse usually writes a letter.
When does the next bus leave?
Who among you is the oldest?
Six hours of work are tiring.
grammar: Шесть часов работы: after 5+, genitive plural. Часов is genitive plural of час. Утомляют is 3rd person plural — the subject часы triggers plural agreement.

english: The girl usually paints a picture.
The musician usually helps a friend.
grammar: Помогать + dative: помогает другу (helps a friend). Обычно signals habitual action, requiring imperfective помогает.

english: Is it possible to change rooms?
grammar: Можно ли = 'is it possible to' — можно is an impersonal word, and ли makes it a polite question.

english: The musician always commutes to work.
The neighbor usually commutes to work.
grammar: Ездить is multidirectional 'to go by transport regularly.' Обычно (usually) pairs with the habitual meaning of ездить.

english: My friend has a country house.
A kind doctor treats sick children.

target: Он ездит на работу на метро.
english: He commutes to work by metro.

target: На работе у него много обязанностей.
english: He has many responsibilities at work.

target: Инженер стирал одежду на прошлой неделе.
english: The engineer did laundry last week.

target: Продавец мыл посуду на прошлой неделе.
english: The salesman washed dishes last week.
grammar: Мыл is past tense masculine of мыть (to wash). На прошлой неделе (last week) signals past tense.

target: Мы понимаем друг друга без слов.
english: We understand each other without words.
grammar: Друг друга means 'each other' — it's a reciprocal pronoun. Без слов = 'without words' uses genitive after без.

target: Я не буду есть эту кашу.
english: I will not eat this porridge.
grammar: Не буду + infinitive is the negative imperfective future: I will not eat. Кашу is accusative of каша.

target: Я не знаю, куда он ушёл.
english: I don't know where he went.
She plans to start a vegetable garden.
May I have a glass of water?
The journalist washes dishes in the evening.
grammar: Мыть посуду means 'to wash dishes' — a common collocation. Вечером (in the evening) uses instrumental case for time of day.

english: The chef rarely works in the office.
The neighbor works in the office soon.
grammar: Скоро (soon) suggests future action, but Russian can use present tense for planned future events.

english: The girl often works in the office.
Which movie do you want to watch?
There are thirty students in our class.
There's nowhere to walk in this city.
grammar: Не- prefix creates opposites: большой → небольшой (big → not big).

english: The farmer paints a picture on Monday.
grammar: В понедельник (on Monday) uses accusative after в for days of the week. Картину is accusative feminine — the direct object of рисует.

target: Я работаю в офисе каждый день.
english: I work in the office every day.
grammar: В офисе uses prepositional after в for location. Каждый день (every day) is an accusative time expression for habitual actions.

target: Медсестра ездит на работу после обеда.
english: The nurse commutes to work after lunch.

target: Продавец ездил на работу на прошлой неделе.
english: The salesman commuted to work last week.
grammar: Ездил is past tense of ездить (multidirectional by vehicle). На прошлой неделе (last week) requires past tense.

target: Москва — самый большой город в России.
english: Moscow is the biggest city in Russia.

target: Дедушка готовит обед в школе после обеда.
english: Grandfather cooks lunch at school after lunch.
grammar: After обеда (after lunch) uses genitive after после. Готовить обед = to cook lunch — обед is accusative as the direct object.

target: Не могли бы вы помочь мне с чемоданом?
english: Could you help me with my suitcase?
There are eleven cars in the parking lot.
How do I get to the metro station?
How many people will come to the party?
Behind the school there is a sports field.
grammar: Позади + genitive means 'behind': позади школы. Спортивная площадка is a compound noun meaning 'sports ground.'

english: There are always many people at the airport.
He is not used to getting up early.

target: Девятнадцатого мая у меня день рождения.
english: My birthday is on the nineteenth of May.

target: Мы вернёмся через неделю, в воскресенье.
english: We will return in a week, on Sunday.

target: Спортсмен иногда читает книгу в школе.
english: The athlete sometimes reads a book at school.
grammar: Иногда (sometimes) indicates occasional action, requiring imperfective aspect: иногда читает (sometimes reads).

target: В квартире три комнаты и кухня.
english: The apartment has three rooms and a kitchen.

target: Мыловар изготовил душистое лавандовое мыло ручной работы.
english: The soap maker produced fragrant handmade lavender soap.

target: Мы планируем посетить Эрмитаж на этих выходных.
english: We plan to visit the Hermitage this weekend.
At the dacha there is a small vegetable garden.

target: Студенты сдают экзамены в конце семестра.
english: Students take exams at the end of the semester.
grammar: Сдавать экзамены means 'to take exams.' В конце + genitive means 'at the end of': в конце семестра.

target: Вышивальщица расшивала крестильную рубашку цветочным орнаментом.
english: The embroiderer embroidered the christening gown with floral ornament.
grammar: Расшивать means 'to embroider.' Цветочным орнаментом uses instrumental to show the pattern used — 'with a floral ornament.'

target: Повар рисует картину в студии сейчас.
english: The chef paints a picture in the studio now.
grammar: The accusative case marks the direct object of a verb.

target: Сестра часто бегает утром на вокзале.
english: Sister often runs in the morning at the station.
grammar: Бегать is multidirectional running (regularly/habitually). Часто (often) pairs with the habitual meaning. Утром = in the morning (instrumental).

target: Студент рисует картину в парке сейчас.
english: The student paints a picture in the park now.
grammar: В парке is prepositional case after в for location. Сейчас (now) marks the present moment — the action is happening right now.

target: Архитектор рисует картину в ресторане в понедельник.
english: The architect paints a picture in the restaurant on Monday.
grammar: В понедельник uses accusative for 'on Monday.' В ресторане uses prepositional for 'in the restaurant' — same preposition в, different cases.

target: Свечница отливала восковые свечи различных форм и размеров.
english: The candlemaker poured wax candles of various shapes and sizes.
grammar: Отливать means 'to cast/mold.' Различных форм и размеров uses genitive plural after a quantity word — 'of various shapes and sizes.'

target: Мама бегала утром в парке на прошлой неделе.
english: Mom ran in the morning at the hospital last week.
grammar: Бегала is past feminine of бегать — the -а ending indicates the feminine subject мама. На прошлой неделе signals past tense.

target: Собака ждёт хозяина у двери каждый вечер.
english: The dog waits for its owner by the door every evening.
grammar: Ждёт + genitive for people: ждёт хозяина (waits for the owner). У двери = by the door. Каждый вечер signals habitual action.

english: Nothing is impossible.
What building is that?
I don't speak Russian.
I don't understand anything.
They don't have children.
grammar: Double negatives are required in Russian: Никто не пришёл = 'Nobody came'.

english: Grandfather rarely does laundry.
Where did you come from?
When does the performance start?
Can I pay by card?
grammar: Можно + infinitive = 'is it possible to.' Расплатиться картой = to pay by card. Instrumental картой expresses the means of payment.

english: When will you return home?
grammar: Когда means 'when' for time questions. Вернёшься is perfective future of вернуться — the perfective form directly becomes future tense.

english: Where does this road lead?
Mom usually writes a letter.
Dad bought a new car.
grammar: Купил is past perfective of купить — a completed one-time purchase. Новую машину is accusative feminine (adjective + noun both change).

english: A quiet building looks wonderful.
grammar: Тихое is neuter nominative agreeing with здание (neuter). Прекрасно is a short-form adjective/adverb meaning 'beautifully/wonderful.'

english: The athlete always buys groceries.
grammar: Всегда (always) signals habitual action requiring imperfective: покупает (buys regularly). Продукты = groceries (always plural).

english: Grandfather sings a song soon.
grammar: Петь (to sing) has a vowel change in conjugation: поёт (3rd person). Песню is accusative of песня — the direct object.

english: The librarian usually buys groceries.
The nurse runs every morning.
grammar: Каждое утро means 'every morning.' Каждый/каждая/каждое agrees in gender with the noun: утро is neuter, so каждое.

english: The driver washes dishes tomorrow.
grammar: Завтра (tomorrow) signals future, but Russian can use present imperfective for scheduled future actions: моет посуду завтра.

english: I am thirty-two years old.
She is twenty-one years old.
She is thirty-two years old.
The salesman often cooks lunch.
The nurse washes dishes now.
A small morning looks wonderful.
Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
What is your shoe size?
What happened to your car?
grammar: Russian can form questions just by intonation—no word order change needed.

english: I don't have free time.
grammar: Нет + genitive expresses absence: нет свободного времени = there is no free time. Both adjective and noun are in genitive.

english: Grandmother usually commutes to work.
Grandmother washes dishes before bed.
Mom calls grandma every evening.
Grandmother has many interesting stories.
One plus one equals two.
grammar: Плюс (plus), минус (minus), равно (equals) are used in math. Один, два, три, четыре, пять are basic cardinal numbers.

english: Dad cooks lunch every day.
How long does the trip take?
grammar: Сколько времени + verb = 'how much time does it take.' Сколько + genitive (времени) asks about quantity.

english: The neighbor rarely dances a waltz.
grammar: Редко (rarely) is a frequency adverb. Танцевать вальс = to dance a waltz — вальс is accusative as the direct object.

english: The farmer usually listens to music.
The driver usually cleans the apartment.
grammar: Обычно (usually) signals habitual action requiring imperfective aspect. Убирать квартиру = to clean the apartment.

english: The farmer rarely listens to music.
The doctor usually listens to music.
Where are you going on vacation?
The artist usually commutes to work.
grammar: Ездить на работу means 'to commute to work.' Обычно (usually) pairs with the multidirectional ездить for regular trips.

english: A winter morning starts with darkness.
grammar: Neuter adjectives: -ое/-ее: новое, синее.

english: The chef washes dishes this morning.
Grandmother writes a letter on Monday.
Mom paints a picture every day.
grammar: Рисовать картину means 'to paint a picture.' Каждый день signals habitual action requiring imperfective рисует.

english: The student washes dishes after lunch.
grammar: После обеда means 'after lunch' — после + genitive. Мыть посуду = to wash dishes, a common daily activity collocation.

english: We need two kilos of potatoes.
The flight takes about three hours.
grammar: Два/две changes by gender: два стула (m.) but две книги (f.).

english: Good afternoon, is this seat free?

target: У каждого человека есть свои мечты.
english: Every person has their own dreams.

target: Он никогда не врёт своим друзьям.
english: He never lies to his friends.

target: Этот магазин не работает по праздникам.
english: This store doesn't work on holidays.
grammar: Не работает means 'doesn't work/is closed.' По праздникам = on holidays — по + dative plural for recurring events.

target: Мало кто знает об этом месте.
english: Few people know about this place.

target: Добрый вечер, как прошёл ваш рабочий день?
english: Good evening, how was your workday?
What is the name of this street?
Inside the box there is a gift.
I have no reason to go there.
grammar: Незачем means 'there's no reason to' — не + за + чем fused together. Ходить here means 'to go' in the general/habitual sense.

english: A large building is visible from afar.
grammar: Neuter nouns typically end in -о/-е: окно, море, поле.

english: See you tomorrow, have a good evening.
Whose umbrella is this on the table?
grammar: Чей means 'whose' and agrees in gender with the noun: чей зонтик (masculine). На столе = on the table (prepositional).

english: There were many people at the concert.
The athlete dances a waltz on weekends.
grammar: По выходным means 'on weekends' — по + dative plural for recurring events. Танцевать вальс = to dance a waltz.

english: The boy often works in the office.
The boy dances a waltz before bed.
grammar: Перед сном means 'before bed' — перед + instrumental. Сон→сном is instrumental of сон (sleep/dream).

english: A beautiful painting hangs on the wall.
grammar: Feminine: -е/-и: школа→в школе, тетрадь→в тетради.

english: The girl paints a picture every day.
The musician usually works in the office.
Twenty students are sitting in the classroom.
The musician paints a picture this morning.
A serious conversation took place yesterday evening.
grammar: Серьёзный is a masculine nominative adjective agreeing with разговор. Вчера вечером = yesterday evening, a common time phrase.

target: Как давно вы живёте в Москве?
english: How long have you lived in Moscow?

target: Водитель ездит на работу перед сном.
english: The driver commutes to work before bed.

target: Я не ем мясо, я вегетарианец.
english: I don't eat meat, I'm a vegetarian.

target: Я не против поехать на море.
english: I'm not against going to the sea.

target: Самый вкусный пирог печёт моя бабушка.
english: My grandmother bakes the most delicious pie.
grammar: Самый вкусный is the superlative: the most delicious. Самый agrees with пирог (masculine). Печёт is from печь (to bake).

target: Для моей семьи это очень важно.
english: This is very important for my family.

target: Фермер пел песню на прошлой неделе.
english: The farmer sang a song last week.

target: Музыкант убирал квартиру на прошлой неделе.
english: The musician cleaned the apartment last week.

target: Рейс номер триста двадцать один задерживается.
english: Flight number three hundred twenty-one is delayed.

target: Наш учитель объясняет правила очень понятно.
english: Our teacher explains the rules very clearly.
grammar: Наш (our) agrees with учитель (masculine). Понятно is an adverb meaning 'clearly' — Russian adverbs don't change form.

target: Три чашки чая для моих гостей.
english: Three cups of tea for my guests.

target: Вы будете читать книгу сегодня вечером.
english: You will read a book this evening.
grammar: Будете читать is imperfective future (буду + infinitive): you will be reading. Сегодня вечером = this evening.

target: Доброе утро, надеюсь, вы хорошо спали.
english: Good morning, I hope you slept well.

target: Добрый вечер, рад вас снова видеть.
english: Good evening, glad to see you again.

target: Мы ни разу не опоздали на работу.
english: We have never been late for work.

target: Бабушка работала в офисе на прошлой неделе.
english: Grandmother worked in the office last week.

target: Ребёнок ездил на работу на прошлой неделе.
english: The child commuted to work last week.
grammar: Ребёнок is an irregular noun — its plural is дети. Ездил is past tense of multidirectional ездить, indicating a past habitual or round trip.

target: Спокойной ночи, приятных снов и хорошего отдыха.
english: Good night, pleasant dreams and good rest.
Could you tell me where the metro is?
grammar: Не подскажете (couldn't you tell) is a polite negative question. Using не in questions paradoxically makes them more polite in Russian.

english: Across from the house there is a playground.
grammar: Быть (to be) is omitted in present tense but required in past and future.

english: There are many antique exhibits in the museum.
There is a wonderful bakery around the corner.
How much does this cost? Two hundred rubles.
grammar: Двести рублей: двести (200) takes genitive plural рублей. Сколько это стоит? = How much does this cost?

english: The beginning of spring is my favorite time.

target: Он не хочет идти в кино.
english: He doesn't want to go to the cinema.

target: Мы не виделись уже три года.
english: We haven't seen each other for three years.

target: Им не разрешили войти без билета.
english: They weren't allowed to enter without a ticket.
grammar: Не разрешили + infinitive = 'didn't allow to.' Без + genitive: без билета = without a ticket.

target: Мне тридцать два года, я инженер.
english: I am thirty-two years old, I'm an engineer.
A quarter to one — lunch is soon.

target: Занятия начинаются в девять часов утра.
english: Classes begin at nine o'clock in the morning.

target: Магазин работает с девяти до девяти.
english: The store is open from nine to nine.

target: Мой номер телефона: восемь девятьсот семнадцать.
english: My phone number is: eight nine hundred seventeen.

target: Экзамен длится три часа без перерыва.
english: The exam lasts three hours without a break.
grammar: After 2,3,4 use genitive singular: два стула. After 5+ use genitive plural: пять стульев.

target: Добрый вечер, погода сегодня просто замечательная!
english: Good evening, the weather today is simply wonderful!

target: Добрый день, я ищу гостиницу поблизости.
english: Good afternoon, I'm looking for a hotel nearby.

target: Добрый день, могу я вам чем-нибудь помочь?
english: Good afternoon, can I help you with something?
grammar: Добрый день = Good afternoon (formal greeting). Могу я = Can I — using я after могу is a polite way to offer help.

english: They chose the child's name for a long time.
grammar: Neuter nouns typically end in -о/-е: окно, море, поле.

english: The new house was built in half a year.
grammar: Построили is past plural perfective — 'they built.' За полгода = within half a year — за + accusative for duration of completion.

english: The new year begins on the first of January.
grammar: After 2,3,4 use genitive singular: два стула. After 5+ use genitive plural: пять стульев.

target: Она не замужем и не собирается.
english: She is not married and doesn't intend to be.
grammar: Никогда не = 'never'; нигде не = 'nowhere'—always paired with не.

target: Музыкант редко танцует вальс на вокзале.
english: The musician rarely dances a waltz at the station.
grammar: На вокзале = at the train station (prepositional). Редко (rarely) is a frequency adverb modifying the habitual verb танцует.

target: Я люблю гулять по набережной вечером.
english: I love walking along the embankment in the evening.
grammar: Гулять по + dative means 'to stroll along': по набережной (along the embankment). Вечером uses instrumental for time of day.

target: Поезд отправляется в восемь тридцать утра.
english: The train departs at eight thirty in the morning.

target: Осталось пять минут до начала фильма.
english: There are five minutes left before the movie starts.
grammar: Dates use ordinal numbers in genitive: первого января = 'of the first of January'.

target: Скажите пожалуйста, во сколько открывается магазин?
english: Tell me please, what time does the store open?
grammar: Пожалуйста means both 'please' and 'you're welcome' depending on context.

target: Учитель рисует картину в магазине скоро.
english: The teacher paints a picture in the store soon.
grammar: В магазине is prepositional for location. Скоро (soon) indicates near future — Russian can use present tense for planned events.

target: Добрый вечер, сегодня прекрасная погода для прогулки.
english: Good evening, today is wonderful weather for a walk.

target: Брат читает книгу в театре по выходным.
english: Brother reads a book in the theater on weekends.

target: Добрый день, я записан на приём к врачу.
english: Good afternoon, I have an appointment with the doctor.

target: Привет всем, я новый сотрудник в вашей команде.
english: Hello everyone, I'm the new employee on your team.

target: Доброе утро, кофе уже готов на столе.
english: Good morning, the coffee is already ready on the table.

target: Доброе утро, можно мне чашку кофе, пожалуйста?
english: Good morning, may I have a cup of coffee, please?

target: Девочка читала книгу в театре на прошлой неделе.
english: The girl read a book in the theater last week.
grammar: Читала is past feminine (agreeing with девочка). На прошлой неделе signals past tense. В театре is prepositional for location.

target: Кондитерская славится своими тортами и миндальным печеньем.
english: The pastry shop is famous for its cakes and almond cookies.

target: Ему двадцать один год, и он только начал последний курс в университете.
english: He is twenty-one years old and has just started his final year at university.
She can't swim.
The homework was difficult.
grammar: Домашнее задание = homework (neuter). Было трудным uses instrumental after быть in past tense: 'was difficult.'

english: Mom always does laundry.
Mom usually sings a song.
grammar: Обычно (usually) signals habitual action. Петь (to sing) conjugates irregularly: пою, поёшь, поёт.

english: He is twenty-five years old.
Two boots make a pair.
grammar: Collective numerals двое, трое, четверо are used with male persons and pluralia tantum nouns.

english: Grandfather rarely sings a song.
Mom usually paints a picture.
She will read a book.
grammar: Будет читать is imperfective future (буду + infinitive) — used for ongoing or habitual future actions: she will be reading.

english: I don't like this movie.
He doesn't work on weekends.
They couldn't solve the problem.
grammar: Не смогли is past plural perfective of смочь (to be able). Решить задачу = to solve a problem (perfective — the solving failed).

english: You shouldn't talk so loudly.

target: Она никогда не жалуется на работу.
english: She never complains about work.
The athlete rarely sings a song.
The girl often sings a song.
grammar: Часто (often) signals habitual action requiring imperfective: поёт (sings). Песню is accusative, the direct object of петь.

english: The journalist usually studies a language.
The chef sometimes sings a song.
grammar: Иногда (sometimes) is a frequency adverb. Повар (cook) is masculine; even female cooks use this form.

english: May I ask you a question?
grammar: Можно + dative + infinitive = 'may I/is it okay to': Можно вам задать вопрос? The dative вам marks the addressee.

english: Today is the twenty-fifth of March.
The farmer picks apples in autumn.
The girl sometimes paints a picture.
Warm milk helps you fall asleep.
The female teacher praises diligent children.
The kitchen smells of fresh baking.
grammar: Masculine/neuter: -е: дом→в доме, окно→в окне.

english: The architect washes dishes before bed.
The salesperson helps customers choose gifts.
The deep sea holds many secrets.
The bus comes every fifteen minutes.
grammar: В (+ prepositional) for months: в январе; but в (+ accusative) for days: в среду.

english: Hello, how are you doing today?
grammar: Здравствуйте is a formal greeting. Ваши дела (your matters) uses the formal/plural possessive ваши — matching the formal вы register.

target: Мы никогда не были в Париже.
english: We have never been to Paris.
grammar: Никогда не были = never have been. Никогда requires double negation with не — both are mandatory in Russian.

target: У меня нет времени на это.
english: I don't have time for this.

target: Я ничего не слышал об этом.
english: I haven't heard anything about this.

target: Мы не согласны с этим решением.
english: We don't agree with this decision.

target: Тебе не стоит волноваться из-за экзамена.
english: You shouldn't worry about the exam.

target: Не могли бы вы закрыть окно?
english: Would you mind closing the window?

target: Архитектор покупал продукты на прошлой неделе.
english: The architect bought groceries last week.

target: Бабушка готовит вкусный суп по воскресеньям.
english: Grandma cooks delicious soup on Sundays.

target: Он нигде не может найти свои ключи.
english: He can't find his keys anywhere.
A fresh apple is in the basket.
grammar: Свежее is neuter nominative agreeing with яблоко. В корзине = in the basket (prepositional). Лежит means 'is lying/located.'

english: A cheerful song plays on the radio.
grammar: Nouns ending in -ь can be masculine or feminine—must be memorized.

english: A kind city stands on the corner.
grammar: Добрый is a masculine nominative adjective agreeing with город. Стоит на углу = stands on the corner — на + prepositional for location.

english: A cheerful park stands on the corner.
grammar: Весёлый is masculine nominative agreeing with парк. Russian adjectives must match noun gender: весёлый парк, весёлая песня, весёлое утро.

english: The middle of summer is vacation time.
grammar: Masculine/neuter genitive: -а/-я: стол→стола, море→моря.

english: The athlete usually works in the office.
There are twenty-five students in the class.
Five children are playing in the yard.
The teacher explained the rule several times.
grammar: Несколько раз means 'several times.' Несколько + genitive plural: несколько раз. Объяснять is imperfective — repeated explanation.

target: Не трогай чужие вещи без разрешения.
english: Don't touch other people's things without permission.
grammar: Не трогай is a negative imperative (informal). Без + genitive: без разрешения = without permission. Чужие = someone else's (plural).

target: Высокое здание построили в прошлом году.
english: A tall building was built last year.
grammar: Plural adjectives: -ые/-ие for all genders: новые, синие.

target: Библиотекарь писал письмо на прошлой неделе.
english: The librarian wrote a letter last week.
grammar: Писал is past masculine of писать, agreeing with библиотекарь (masculine). На прошлой неделе indicates past tense.

target: Продавец пел песню на прошлой неделе.
english: The salesman sang a song last week.

target: Она слушает классическую музыку каждый вечер.
english: She listens to classical music every evening.
grammar: Классическую музыку is accusative feminine — both adjective and noun change. Слушать takes accusative for what you listen to.

target: Журналист обычно готовит обед в школе.
english: The journalist usually cooks lunch at school.
grammar: The accusative case marks the direct object of a verb.

target: Ребёнок ездит на работу каждый вечер.
english: The child commutes to work every evening.
grammar: Ездить на работу = to commute to work. На + accusative for direction: на работу. Каждый вечер = every evening.

target: Он заказал горячий суп в ресторане.
english: He ordered hot soup at the restaurant.

target: Я приехал из Москвы две недели назад.
english: I arrived from Moscow two weeks ago.

target: Ни ты, ни я не знаем правду.
english: Neither you nor I know the truth.
grammar: Ни...ни means 'neither...nor': Ни ты, ни я. Double negation is required: не знаем pairs with ни...ни.

english: This is the fifth chapter of the book.
grammar: Пятая is an ordinal number (fifth) agreeing with глава (feminine). Ordinals decline like adjectives: пятая глава, пятой главы.

english: A strong wind is blowing from the sea.
grammar: С + genitive means 'from': с моря = from the sea. Дуть (to blow) is first conjugation: дует (blows).

target: Бабушка вяжет тёплый шарф для внука.
english: Grandmother knits a warm scarf for her grandson.

target: Папа часто читает книгу в театре.
english: Dad often reads a book in the theater.
grammar: Adjectives must agree with nouns in gender, number, and case.

target: Я не понимаю, можете повторить, пожалуйста?
english: I don't understand, can you repeat that please?

target: Мы забронировали двухместный номер в отеле.
english: We booked a double room at the hotel.

target: Водитель обычно готовит обед на вокзале.
english: The driver usually cooks lunch at the station.

target: Мама рисует картину на рынке завтра.
english: Mom paints a picture at the market tomorrow.

target: Сосед плавал в бассейне на прошлой неделе.
english: The neighbor swam in the pool last week.
grammar: Плавать is multidirectional swimming — used for habitual activity: плавал в бассейне = used to swim in the pool.

target: Русский язык — один из самых сложных.
english: Russian is one of the most difficult languages.

target: Мой номер телефона записан в этой тетради.
english: My phone number is written in this notebook.
grammar: Записан is a short passive participle: is written down. В этой тетради = in this notebook (prepositional). Мой номер = my number.

english: It takes forty minutes to drive to the airport.
grammar: В (+ prepositional) for months: в январе; but в (+ accusative) for days: в среду.

english: The teacher explains a difficult topic to the students.
grammar: Объяснять + accusative (тему) + dative (ученикам): to explain the topic to the students. Dative marks the recipients.

target: Студент редко рисует картину в театре.
english: The student rarely paints a picture in the theater.
grammar: The accusative case marks the direct object of a verb.

target: Ребёнок иногда читает книгу на вокзале.
english: The child sometimes reads a book at the station.
grammar: Иногда (sometimes) signals occasional action requiring imperfective. На вокзале = at the station (prepositional after на).

target: Токарь выточил деревянную чашу на токарном станке.
english: The turner shaped a wooden bowl on the lathe.

target: Я учусь в университете на третьем курсе.
english: I study at the university in the third year.

target: Брат читает книгу в магазине сегодня утром.
english: Brother reads a book in the store this morning.
grammar: Сегодня утром = this morning. В магазине is prepositional for location. Книгу is accusative — the direct object of читает.

target: Три раза в неделю я хожу в спортзал.
english: Three times a week I go to the gym.
grammar: Три раза в неделю = three times a week. Ходить в спортзал = to go to the gym (habitual). В + accusative for direction.

target: Садовник посадил лаванду и подсолнухи в палисаднике.
english: The gardener planted lavender and sunflowers in the front garden.

target: Двадцать третьего февраля — День защитника Отечества.
english: The twenty-third of February is Defender of the Fatherland Day.
grammar: Cardinal numbers decline by case in formal Russian.

target: Девочка играет в шахматы на рынке вечером.
english: The girl plays chess at the market in the evening.
grammar: The accusative case marks the direct object of a verb.

target: Медсестра пишет письмо на рынке после обеда.
english: The nurse writes a letter at the market after lunch.
grammar: На рынке = at the market (prepositional for location). После обеда = after lunch (после + genitive).

target: Здравствуйте, меня зовут Иван, очень приятно познакомиться.
english: Hello, my name is Ivan, very nice to meet you.

target: Почтальон ехал на велосипеде под дождём с полной сумкой.
english: The postman cycled through the rain with a full bag.

target: Извините, вы не подскажете, где находится ближайшая аптека?
english: Excuse me, could you tell me where the nearest pharmacy is?
grammar: Adding -те to imperatives makes them polite: скажи → скажите.

target: Добрый день, вы не подскажете дорогу к метро?
english: Good afternoon, could you tell me the way to the metro?
grammar: Adding -те to imperatives makes them polite: скажи → скажите.

target: В году двенадцать месяцев и триста шестьдесят пять дней.
english: There are twelve months and three hundred sixty-five days in a year.
grammar: Cardinal numbers decline by case in formal Russian.

target: Они строили дом два года и наконец построили его.
english: They were building a house for two years and finally built it.
Good night, sweet dreams!
Small children love sweets.
She often cooks at home.
grammar: Часто (often) at the start shifts emphasis to frequency. Дома means 'at home' — it's a special locative form, not regular prepositional.

english: A new sea looks wonderful.
A old window looks wonderful.
grammar: Neuter adjective endings: -ое/-ее (nom./acc.), otherwise like masculine.

english: A big letter looks wonderful.
A strong morning looks wonderful.
The engineer always plays chess.
Let's drink to your health!
grammar: Давайте + perfective = 'let's' for a specific occasion: Давайте выпьем! За + accusative in toasts: за здоровье = to your health!

english: Sister cooks lunch before bed.
The salesman sometimes cleans the apartment.
grammar: Иногда (sometimes) signals occasional habitual action. Убирать квартиру = to clean the apartment (imperfective for repeated action).

english: I am reading an interesting book.
We live on the fifth floor.
The postman delivers letters every day.
Many tourists come here in summer.
Grandfather usually washes dishes at home.
grammar: Обычно (usually) signals habitual action. Дома is a locative adverb meaning 'at home' — it doesn't decline like a regular noun.

english: Good luck on your exam tomorrow!
A happy mother hugs her child.
I live in a big city.

target: Мы начинали эту работу много раз.
english: We started this work many times.

target: Эта куртка стоит пять тысяч рублей.
english: This jacket costs five thousand roubles.
grammar: Numbers 1-10 must be memorized: один, два, три, четыре, пять, шесть, семь, восемь, девять, десять.

target: Она едет на работу на автобусе.
english: She goes to work by bus.
grammar: На автобусе = by bus — на + prepositional for means of transport. На работу = to work — на + accusative for direction.

target: Он любит свою жену и детей.
english: He loves his wife and children.
grammar: Свой refers back to the subject: он любит свою жену = he loves his (own) wife. Use свой, not его, when the possessor is the subject.

target: Новые студенты пришли в наш класс.
english: New students came to our class.

target: Дедушка ездил на работу на прошлой неделе.
english: Grandfather commuted to work last week.
grammar: Ездил is past of multidirectional ездить — a completed round trip or habitual past. На прошлой неделе = last week.

english: The girl dances at her ballet lesson.
The neighbor dances a waltz on Monday.
I didn't manage to buy a gift.
An old tree grows near the river.
An interesting exhibition opened at the museum.
A short skirt is in fashion now.
The taxi took us to the hotel.
The nurse cooks lunch at home now.

target: Она рисует портреты в свободное время.
english: She draws portraits in her free time.

target: Сестра рисует красивые картины каждый день.
english: My sister paints beautiful pictures every day.

target: Старые друзья встретились после долгой разлуки.
english: Old friends met after a long separation.
grammar: Старые друзья = old friends (plural nominative). После + genitive: после долгой разлуки = after a long separation.

target: Сестра готовила обед дома на прошлой неделе.
english: Sister cooked lunch at home last week.
Take care of yourself and get some rest.
grammar: Береги is an informal imperative of беречь (to take care of). Себя is the reflexive pronoun 'yourself' — it has no nominative form.

english: It's half past nine — time to go.
grammar: Russian uses 24-hour time in formal contexts: 14:00 = два часа дня.

english: An important decision needs to be made today.

target: Папа ведёт машину через весь город.
english: Dad drives the car through the entire city.
grammar: Вести машину means 'to drive a car.' Вести is unidirectional — driving in one direction right now. Через + accusative = across.

target: Продавец часто покупает продукты в парке.
english: The salesman often buys groceries in the park.
grammar: Часто (often) signals habitual action. Покупать продукты = to buy groceries — a common imperfective collocation for regular shopping.

target: Брат всегда убирает квартиру на пляже.
english: Brother always cleans the apartment at the beach.
grammar: Всегда (always) indicates permanent habitual action. Убирать квартиру = to clean the apartment.

target: Новая книга очень важна для меня.
english: A new book is very important to me.
grammar: Masculine adjectives: -ый/-ий/-ой: новый, синий, большой.

target: Сильный дождь идёт уже два часа.
english: Heavy rain has been falling for two hours.
grammar: Уже два часа = already for two hours. Идти for rain: дождь идёт literally means 'rain goes' — the standard way to say it's raining.

target: Мы перевезли мебель на новую квартиру.
english: We transported the furniture to the new apartment.

target: Мама помогает другу в парке сейчас.
english: Mom helps a friend in the park now.
grammar: Помогать + dative: помогает другу = helps a friend. Сейчас (now) marks present continuous action.

target: Папа помогает другу на вокзале сейчас.
english: Dad helps a friend at the station now.
grammar: На вокзале = at the train station (prepositional after на). Помогать requires dative: помогает другу.

target: Мама рисует картину в ресторане завтра.
english: Mom paints a picture in the restaurant tomorrow.

target: В нашем городе проживает пятьсот тысяч человек.
english: Five hundred thousand people live in our city.

target: Мы отъехали от города на сто километров.
english: We drove a hundred kilometers from the city.
grammar: Отъехать means 'to drive away from.' Prefix от- means 'away from': от города = from the city. На сто километров = by 100 km.

target: Закройте дверь за собой, когда будете уходить.
english: Close the door behind you when you leave.
grammar: За собой means 'behind/after yourself.' Когда будете уходить = when you leave — будете + imperfective for future action.

target: Зимой мы всегда пьём чай с мёдом.
english: We always drink tea with honey in winter.

target: Суп должен ещё час потомиться на огне.
english: The soup needs to simmer for another hour.
